chunks: Al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام used to advise his children and say:

When the month of Ramadan enters, then exert yourselves, for in it sustenances are apportioned, lifespans are written, and in it the delegation of Allah—those who come unto Him—is recorded; and in it is a night in which action is better than action in a thousand months.

key_terms.أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ: a thousand months, indicating immense multiplied value
key_terms.الْآجَالُ: appointed lifespans or terms of life
key_terms.الْأَرْزَاقُ: sustenances and provisions apportioned by Allah
key_terms.شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the sacred month of fasting and intensified worship
key_terms.فَأَجْهِدُوا: strive with full effort; exert yourselves seriously in worship
key_terms.لَيْلَةٌ: a night of special distinction within Ramadan
key_terms.وَفْدُ اللَّهِ: the delegation of Allah, those who come as honored visitors unto Him

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teach about striving in the month of Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith is an exhortation from Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام to make full spiritual effort in the month of Ramadan. It highlights Ramadan as a divinely significant time in which provisions and lifespans are decreed, and which contains a night whose deeds surpass those of a thousand months.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1842 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) used to advise his children, saying:

"When the Month of Ramadan begins, strive with all your effort, for in it sustenance is distributed, lifespans are decreed, and the delegation to Allah (swt) - those who journey toward Him, is recorded. In it is a night wherein deeds performed are better than deeds done in a thousand months."
